outcomes.name: Six-minute walking distance, change from baseline
outcomes.definition: Every contributing registration declares this primary, so the OUTCOME limb passes. That is why an outcome-only screen passed this page and why it is not poolable on a different limb.

six_minute_walk.poolable_reason: THE TWO TRIALS ARE IN TWO DIFFERENT DISEASES. Read from ClinicalTrials.gov 2026-08-18: NCT00810693 enrols PULMONARY ARTERIAL HYPERTENSION and NCT00855465 enrols CHRONIC THROMBOEMBOLIC PULMONARY HYPERTENSION. Both test riociguat against placebo and both register a six-minute-walk primary -- so the intervention, comparator and outcome limbs all pass, and an outcome-only screen passed this page. THE PARTICIPANTS LIMB FAILS. CTEPH is a different disease from PAH, with a different mechanism and different management, and this topic is titled for PAH. THE ENDPOINTS ALSO SIT AT DIFFERENT TIMEPOINTS: week 12 against week 16. FOR THE QUESTION THE TITLE ASKS, THIS IS k=1, and a single trial is reported as a single trial, not pooled.

six_minute_walk.what_this_verdict_does_not_establish: NOT that the trials are poor -- each is registered, randomised and reports its primary. NOT that the drug is ineffective. NOT that no poolable question exists in this area -- only that the one this page's title asks cannot be answered by pooling the trials on it.
